areas.name: Sacagawea Peak
areas.blurb: Sacagawea Peak is the highest summit in the Bridger Range, rising above Fairy Lake north of Bozeman. A short, steep trail reaches its summit from the east, while its rocky east face and ribs offer easy fifth-class scrambling and snow chutes that hold into early summer.

routes.name: Sacagawea Direct
routes.rock_grade: Easy fifth-class slab, then 3rd-4th class rib
routes.best_season: Mid-July through September, once the road is open and the east-side gullies have melted out
routes.overview: A direct line up the east side of the highest peak in the Bridger Range, starting from the bowl between Hardscrabble and Sacagawea. An intimidating but easy fifth-class slab leads onto a long rib between two gullies, which climbs straight toward the summit ridge. It is a short, steep alternative to the hiking trail, with the trail itself as the descent.
routes.beta: Start at the base of the obvious slab at the foot of the peak, in the bowl between Hardscrabble and Sacagawea. The slab is the crux: roughly 50 m of easy fifth-class climbing at about 55 degrees on good rock, but it is steep and continuous enough that a fall would not stop, so climb it deliberately or rope up. Above the slab, follow the rib that runs between two gullies for roughly 175 m at a gentler angle, mostly 3rd and 4th class, staying on the crest rather than dropping into the loose gullies on either side. The rib tops out near the summit ridge; a short ridge walk leads to the summit.
routes.approach: From the Fairy Lake Trailhead, take the Sacagawea Pass trail west through forest and into open meadows below the peak. Leave the trail in the upper basin and cross talus into the bowl between Hardscrabble and Sacagawea, aiming for the base of the slab at the foot of Sacagawea's east side.
routes.descent_text: From the summit, follow the ordinary trail north down the ridge to the saddle (the pass on the Bridger Divide), then switchback east down the Sacagawea Pass trail back to the Fairy Lake Trailhead.
routes.turnaround: Turn around if the slab is wet, icy or snow-covered, or if thunderstorms are building over the range; the rib is an exposed place to be caught in lightning.
routes.bail: Below the slab, simply walk back to the trail. Once on the rib, the gullies on either side are loose and not a good escape; continuing up the rib to the summit ridge and descending the trail is usually the quickest way off.

pitch_detail.notes: Trail from Fairy Lake Trailhead toward the pass, then off-trail across talus into the bowl between Hardscrabble and Sacagawea.
About 50 m at roughly 55 degrees. Good rock but continuous and no place for a fall; the crux.
About 175 m at roughly 45 degrees along the rib between two gullies. Stay on the crest.
Exit the rib and walk the short ridge to the summit.
Summit trail north to the saddle, then the Sacagawea Pass trail back to Fairy Lake.

gear: Optional short rope and a few pieces for the slab
hazards: Unprotected slab where a fall would be serious
Loose rock in the gullies beside the rib
Lingering snow in the east-side chutes into early summer
obj_haz: Snow and ice in the gullies early in the season
routes.watch_out:
The slab is steeper than it looks from the bowl and does not forgive a slip
Do not drift into the gullies beside the rib; the rock there is loose
Mountain goats frequent the summit area; give them space
pro_tips: Start early to be off the rib before afternoon storms
Climb the slab only when it is completely dry
Stay on the crest of the rib for the best rock
Check the Fairy Lake Road status before driving up

road.name: Fairy Lake Road (Forest Road 74)
road.driveNote: Turn off Bridger Canyon Road (Highway 86) north of Bozeman onto Fairy Lake Road, then climb about 6 miles of steep, rough gravel to the trailhead. It is passable for most 2WD cars when dry but can be impassable without 4WD when muddy or snowy. The road is closed seasonally in winter and spring (usually through the end of June), and road improvement work began in spring 2026, so expect delays or closures; check with the Bozeman Ranger District before going.

timing.recommendedStart: Early morning, to be off the rib before afternoon thunderstorms

rack: Short rope and a light rack (optional, for the slab)

access.land_manager: Custer Gallatin National Forest (Bozeman Ranger District)
